Apple Inc. (AAPL) Short Interest Up 16.8% in February Posted by Caroline Horne | Mar 3rd, 2018 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) was the recipient of a significant growth in short interest during the month of February. As of February 15th, there was short interest totalling 49,152,571 shares, a growth of 16.8% from the January 31st total of 42,078,757 shares. Based on an average trading volume of 58,301,658 shares, the days-to-cover ratio is presently 0.8 days. Approximately 1.0% of the shares of the stock are sold short. 
A number of research analysts recently issued reports on AAPL shares. Citigroup reiterated a “buy” rating and issued a $200.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a report on Wednesday, December 13th. Bank of America lowered shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “neutral” rating and raised their price objective for the company from $180.00 to $220.00 in a report on Wednesday, January 17th. Cascend Securities raised their price objective on shares of Apple from $200.00 to $220.00 and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Monday, January 29th. Nomura set a $185.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Monday, November 27th. Finally, UBS Group reiterated a “buy” rating and issued a $190.00 price objective (up previously from $180.00) on shares of Apple in a report on Friday, November 3rd. One equities research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-four have assigned a buy rating and one has assigned a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. The stock presently has a consensus rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $201.58. Get Apple alerts: 
In other news, insider Daniel J. Riccio sold 15,641 shares of the stock in a transaction dated Friday, January 5th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.78, for a total value of $2,733,733.98. Following the completion of the transaction, the insider now owns 13,739 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $2,401,302.42. The transaction was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which can be accessed through this hyperlink . 0.08% of the stock is currently owned by corporate insiders. 
Several hedge funds and other institutional investors have recently added to or reduced their stakes in AAPL. Honkamp Krueger Financial Services Inc. increased its holdings in Apple by 8.1% in the 2nd quarter. Honkamp Krueger Financial Services Inc. now owns 63,703 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $9,175,000 after acquiring an additional 4,777 shares during the last quarter. Pillar Pacific Capital Management LLC increased its holdings in Apple by 5.5% in the 2nd quarter. Pillar Pacific Capital Management LLC now owns 98,104 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $14,130,000 after acquiring an additional 5,143 shares during the last quarter. Cardinal Capital Management increased its holdings in Apple by 2.9% in the 2nd quarter. Cardinal Capital Management now owns 41,097 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,919,000 after acquiring an additional 1,160 shares during the last quarter. Mitchell Capital Management Co. increased its holdings in Apple by 3.6% in the 2nd quarter. Mitchell Capital Management Co. now owns 2,831 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $408,000 after acquiring an additional 98 shares during the last quarter. Finally, CIBC Asset Management Inc increased its holdings in Apple by 2.2% in the 2nd quarter. CIBC Asset Management Inc now owns 746,619 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $107,528,000 after acquiring an additional 16,031 shares during the last quarter. Institutional investors own 59.70% of the company’s stock. 
Apple ( AAPL ) opened at $176.21 on Friday. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a current ratio of 1.24. Apple has a 52 week low of $137.05 and a 52 week high of $180.62. The firm has a market capitalization of $894,090.00, a price-to-earnings ratio of 17.24, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.34 and a beta of 1.22. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last issued its quarterly earnings data on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a return on equity of 37.37% and a net margin of 21.13%. The business had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $87.62 billion. During the same period last year, the business earned $3.36 EPS. The business’s revenue was up 12.7% on a year-over-year basis. equities research analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.43 earnings per share for the current year. 
The firm also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, February 15th. Stockholders of record on Monday, February 12th were paid a dividend of $0.63 per share. This represents a $2.52 dividend on an annualized basis and a dividend yield of 1.43%. The ex-dividend date was Friday, February 9th. Apple’s payout ratio is 24.66%.
